'''Kevin Marquis Murphy''' (born March 6, 1990) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Sagesse SC|Sagesse Club]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]]. He played college basketball for the [[Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles men's basketball|Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles]].

==High school career==
Born in [[Atlanta]],<ref name=TennesseeBio>{{cite web|url=http://www.ttusports.com/sports/mbkb/2011-12/bios/murphy_kevin|title=55 – Kevin Murphy|access-date=June 29, 2012}}</ref> Murphy earned four varsity letters in basketball at [[Creekside High School (Fairburn, Georgia)|Creekside High School]] in [[Fairburn, Georgia]]. In his senior season at Creekside High School, Murphy averaged 26 points, 8 rebounds and 3 assists per game.<ref name=TennesseeBio />

==College career==

===Freshman season===
In his freshman season at [[Tennessee Tech]], Murphy averaged 9.6 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 1.8 assists per game.<ref name=TennesseeBio />

===Sophomore season===
As a sophomore, Murphy averaged 15.3 points per game, 3.9 rebounds, and 2.0 assists per game. He was awarded the Best Offensive Player Award by head coach [[Mike Sutton (basketball)|Mike Sutton]].<ref name=TennesseeBio />

===Junior season===
In his junior year, Murphy averaged 17.0 points, 4.5 rebounds, and 1.7 assists per game. In the [[Ohio Valley Conference men's basketball tournament]], Murphy averaged 24.3 points per game and was named to the All-Tournament Team. Murphy was also an All-OVC first team selection.<ref name=TennesseeBio />

===Senior season===
On January 30, 2012, Murphy scored 50 points in a win over [[SIU Edwardsville Cougars men's basketball|SIU Edwardsville]], the most for any Division I player in the [[2011-12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=SIU-Edwardsville Cougars vs. Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles recap|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=320302635|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230330205026/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=320302635|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 30, 2023|work=[[ESPN]]|access-date=4 July 2012}}</ref> Murphy averaged 20.6 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 2.3 assists per game during the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kevin Murphy stats|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/6613/kevin-murphy|work=[[ESPN]]|access-date=4 July 2012}}</ref> He was also named to the OVC All-Tournament Team and the All-OVC first team for the second consecutive year.<ref name=TennesseeBio /> Following the season, Murphy participated in the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]]. He was named to the All-Tournament Team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Portsmouth Invitational Tournament|url=http://www.portsmouthinvitational.com/|access-date=14 July 2012}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Murphy was selected with the 47th overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]] by the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/20120628-draft-kevin-murphy.html|title=Utah Jazz Selects Kevin Murphy in Second Round of 2012 NBA Draft|website=www.nba.com}}</ref> He joined the Jazz for the 2012 NBA Summer League. On November 26, 2012, Murphy was assigned to the [[Reno Bighorns]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA D-League]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/utah_jazz_assign_rookie_kevin_murphy_to_reno_bighorns_2012_11_24.html |title=Utah Jazz Assign Rookie Kevin Murphy to NBA D-League Affiliate Reno Bighorns |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2013-01-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130101182956/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/utah_jazz_assign_rookie_kevin_murphy_to_reno_bighorns_2012_11_24.html |archive-date=2013-01-01 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On January 8, 2013, the Jazz recalled him from the D-League.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-recalls-kevin-murphy-d-league|title=Jazz Recalls Kevin Murphy from D-League|website=www.nba.com}}</ref> On July 10, 2013, Murphy was involved in a three-team trade that sent him and [[Andre Iguodala]], then of the [[Denver Nuggets]], to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-acquire-andre-iguodala-071013|title=Warriors Acquire Andre Iguodala from Denver Nuggets as Part of Three-Team Trade|work=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2013|access-date=July 10, 2013}}</ref> He joined the Warriors for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. On July 24, 2013, Murphy was waived by the Warriors.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/golden-state-warriors-waive-dwayne-jones-scott-machado-and-kevin-murphy-0|title=Golden State Warriors Waive Dwayne Jones, Scott Machado and Kevin Murphy|website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref>

On August 11, 2013, he signed with [[SIG Basket|Strasbourg IG]] of France.<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/france/61345/strasbourg-officially-sign-kevin-murphy.html Strasbourg officially sign Kevin Murphy]</ref> On December 25, 2013, he left Strasbourg.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kevin Murphy leaves SIG Strasbourg|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/france/70293/kevin-murphy-leaves-sig-strasbourg.html|access-date=December 30, 2013|work=Sportando.net|date=December 25, 2013}}</ref> On January 4, 2014, he was acquired by the [[Idaho Stampede]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/stampede_acquire_kevin_murphy_2014_01_06.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222070639/http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/stampede_acquire_kevin_murphy_2014_01_06.html|url-status=dead|title=Stampede Acquire Kevin Murphy|website=[[NBA.com]] |archive-date=February 22, 2014}}</ref>

On August 27, 2014, he signed with the Utah Jazz.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-signs-free-agent-kevin-murphy|title=Jazz Signs Free Agent Kevin Murphy|website=www.nba.com}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Jazz on October 10, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-waive-guards-bost-and-murphy|title=Jazz Waive Guards Bost and Murphy|website=www.nba.com}}</ref> On November 3, 2014, he was reacquired by the Idaho Stampede.<ref>{{cite news|title=2014 Training Camp Roster |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/2014_training_camp_roster_2014_11_03.html |access-date=November 11, 2014 |work=NBA.com |date=November 3, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141106165958/http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/2014_training_camp_roster_2014_11_03.html |archive-date=November 6, 2014 }}</ref> On December 30, 2014, he left the Stampede after appearing in 15 games.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/d-league/146839/kevin-murphy-leaves-idaho-stampede.html|title=Kevin Murphy leaves Idaho Stampede}}</ref> On January 2, 2015, he signed with the [[Zhejiang Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/147114/kevin-murphy-signs-in-china-with-zhejiang-guangsha.html|title=Kevin Murphy signs in China with Zhejiang Guangsha}}</ref> Following the conclusion of the CBA season, he returned to the United States, and on February 19, he was reacquired by the Stampede.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/kevin-murphy-returns-to-stampede/n-4928964|title=Kevin Murphy Returns to Stampede|date=February 19, 2015|website=OurSports Central}}</ref> On February 26, he was traded to the [[Grand Rapids Drive]] in exchange for Brandon Fields.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/grand-rapids-drive-trades-willie-reed-diante-garrett-brandon-fields-kevin-murphy-stampede-energy-022615/|title=Grand Rapids Drive Make Two Trades, Acquire Diante Garrett and Kevin Murphy|work=NBA.com|date=February 26, 2015|access-date=February 26, 2015}}</ref>

On November 8, 2015, Murphy signed with the [[Hitachi SunRockers]] of the [[Japan Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/Japan/news/427385/Kevin-Murphy-signs-at-Hitachi-Sunrockers|title=Kevin Murphy signs at Hitachi Sunrockers|work=Asia-Basket.com|date=November 8, 2015|access-date=November 8, 2015}}</ref>

On September 8, 2016, Murphy signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-six-free-agents-training-camp-nick-johnson-cliff-alexander-damjan-rudez-20160908|title=Orlando Magic Sign Six Players|date=September 8, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 8, 2016}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Magic on October 16 after appearing in two preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-alexander-dawson-murphy|title=Magic Waive Alexander, Dawson, Murphy|work=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2016|access-date=October 16, 2016}}</ref> On November 17, 2016, Murphy was reacquired by the Grand Rapids Drive.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/drive-acquire-kevin-murphy/n-5216259|title=Drive Acquire Kevin Murphy|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 17, 2016|access-date=November 20, 2016}}</ref>

On April 22, 2017, Murphy signed with [[Guangxi Rhinos]] of the Chinese [[National Basketball League (China)|National Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidebasketeurope.com/actu/murphy-guangxi.html|title=Kevin Murphy - ex SIG - signe en Chine|work=insidebasketeurope.com|date=April 22, 2017|access-date=April 22, 2017|archive-date=April 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170422212040/http://www.insidebasketeurope.com/actu/murphy-guangxi.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> On July 19, 2017, Murphy scored a career-high 67 points to go along with 6 rebounds in a 118–132 loss to the Lhasa Pure Land.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2017/0719_20528_15108.asp|title=Lhasa Pure Land 132 - Guangxi Rhinos 118|publisher=EuroBasket|date=July 19, 2017|access-date=June 25, 2020}}</ref>

On August 5, 2017, Murphy signed with Croatian club [[KK Cedevita|Cedevita Zagreb]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Cedevita signed with American sharp-shooter Kevin Murphy|url=http://www.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=38533|access-date=August 5, 2017|work=aba-liga.com|date=August 5, 2017}}</ref> On January 20, 2018, he parted ways with Cedevita.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news/39700|title=Cedevita parted ways with Murphy : ABA League|first=ABA liga|last=j.t.d|website=ABA Liga}}</ref> On September 26, 2018, Murphy signed with the [[San Miguel Beermen]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA).<ref>{{cite news|title=San Miguel parting ways with AZ Reid as Kevin Murphy comes in|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/san-miguel-parting-ways-with-az-reid-as-kevin-murphy-comes-in-a793-20180926?ref=feed_2_section|access-date=September 26, 2018|work=spin.ph|date=September 26, 2018}}</ref>

In 2022, Kevin Murphy was named the Season 5 [[BIG3]] MVP.

In October 2022, Murphy played for Kuwaiti club [[Kazma SC (basketball)|Kazma]] in the [[2022 Arab Club Basketball Championship]]. On October 12, in the quarterfinals, he scored 53 points in a 106–101 overtime win over [[Al Ittihad Alexandria (basketball)|Al Ittihad Alexandria]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=asia-basket |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/boxScores/Arab%20Club%20Championships/2022/1012_2859_6004.asp. |access-date=2022-10-14 |website=www.asia-basket.com}}</ref>

In February 2023, Murphy returned to the Philippines, this time signing with the [[NorthPort Batang Pier]] to replace [[Marcus Weathers]] as the team's import for the [[2023 PBA Governors' Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Li|first=Matthew|url=https://tiebreakertimes.com.ph/tbt/northport-brings-in-ex-smb-import-murphy-to-replace-weathers/261345|title=Northport brings in ex-SMB import Murphy to replace Weathers|publisher= Tiebreaker Times|date=February 7, 2023|access-date=February 7, 2023}}</ref>

In February 2024, Murphy joined [[Al-Ahly Ly SC (basketball)|Al Ahly Ly]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Kevin Murphy (ex Ittihad) is a newcomer at Ahly Benghazi |url=https://www.afrobasket.com/Libya/news/855297/Kevin-Murphy-ex-Ittihad-is-a-newcomer-at-Ahly-Benghazi |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=11 November 2024 |date=22 February 2024}}</ref> On April 19, 2024, Murphy made his debut for Al Ahly Ly in the [[Basketball Africa League]] (BAL). He had 21 points, 5 rebounds and 6 assists in their opening day win over [[Bangui Sporting Club]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Al Ahly Ly vs. Bangui SC |url=https://fibalivestats.dcd.shared.geniussports.com/u/BAL/2410678/bs.html |access-date=2024-04-19}}</ref>

In October 2024, Murphy joined another Libyan club in [[Al Ahli Tripoli (basketball)|Al Ahli Tripoli]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Kevin Murphy (ex Beirut Club) agreed terms with Ahly Tripoli |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Lebanon/news/898798/Kevin-Murphy-ex-Beirut-Club-agreed-terms-with-Ahly-Tripoli |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=11 November 2024 |date=29 October 2024}}</ref> for the [[2025 BAL qualification]]. On November 9, 2024, he scored 34 points in the decisive victory of Tripoli over the [[ABC Fighters]], which clinched the team's first BAL participation in club history.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-09 |title=Murphy's 34 points send Al Ahli Tripoli to the 2025 BAL |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-africa-champions-clubs-road-to-bal-2025/news/murphys-34-points-send-al-ahli-tripoli-to-the-2025-bal |access-date=2024-11-10 |website=www.fiba.basketball |language=en}}</ref>
